app.name: Panda Tweaks
app.tagline: Free Windows tweaking, with nothing hidden
risk.safe.help: Very low risk. Easy to reverse and does not affect how Windows works.
risk.advanced.help: Changes system behaviour. Reversible, but read what it does first.
risk.risky.help: Can weaken security or break features. Off by default and never recommended automatically.
dashboard.neverScanned: Your system has not been analysed yet.
dashboard.scanningHint: Reading settings only — nothing is being changed.
dashboard.scanFailed: The analysis could not be completed.
dashboard.noRecommendations: Nothing to recommend — your system already matches what we would suggest.
recommended.title: Recommended for your system
recommended.subtitle: Based on what the analysis actually found on this machine.
recommended.empty: No recommendations. Either everything is already in place, or your system does not need these changes.
reason.generallyRecommended: Generally recommended and not currently active
reason.gamingHardware: This machine has gaming hardware that benefits from it
reason.privacyLow: Your privacy score has room to improve
reason.manyPreinstalled: A lot of preinstalled apps and startup entries were found
reason.performanceLow: Your performance score has room to improve
skipped.title: Left out on this machine
skipped.subtitle: These would have been suggested, but something about your PC says otherwise.
skipped.risky: Risky — never applied automatically, switch it on in Settings if you want it
skipped.laptopBattery: This is a laptop — keeping the hardware awake would cost more battery than it gains you
tweaks.title: All tweaks
tweaks.subtitle: {count} tweaks. Every one shows exactly what it changes.
tweaks.riskyHidden: Risky tweaks are hidden. You can show them in Settings.
apply.title: You are about to apply {count} tweaks.
apply.restoreRecommended: A system restore point is recommended before applying these changes.
apply.riskyWarning: You have selected risky tweaks. These can weaken Windows security features or break functionality.
apply.needsAdminWarning: {count} of these need administrator rights. Restart as administrator to apply them.
apply.restartNeeded: Some changes need a restart to take effect.
debloat.title: Debloat
debloat.subtitle: Preinstalled apps and optional components found on this system.
debloat.keepWarning: Careful: {names} is part of Windows and other features rely on it. Getting it back means reinstalling from the Microsoft Store.
debloat.absentCount: {n} catalogue entries you do not have installed
debloat.group.components.hint: Removing these can break video, games or the Store
debloat.notReversibleWarning: Removal applies to your account only. Undo in the history usually puts an app back — that needs administrator rights, and Windows still has to have the files. Otherwise it is the Microsoft Store.
system.title: System information
history.title: History
history.subtitle: Every change Panda Tweaks made, and what it can put back.
history.empty: No changes have been made yet.
history.undoConfirm: This restores the values that were in place before this tweak was applied.
history.undoFailed: Could not restore the previous state.
settings.title: Settings
settings.askRestore: Ask about a restore point before applying tweaks
settings.showRisky: Show risky tweaks in the tweak list
settings.showRiskyHelp: Risky tweaks stay off by default even when shown.
settings.resetConfirm: This resets appearance and safety options. Your applied tweaks and history are kept.
settings.noTelemetry: Panda Tweaks collects nothing and sends nothing. All files stay on this PC.
about.title: About Panda Tweaks
about.free: Free and open source, with no telemetry and no account.
about.licenseBody: Released under the MIT Licence. The full licence text and third-party notices ship with the application.
about.dataLocation: Your settings, history and log are stored in
restore.title: System restore point
restore.body: Before applying system tweaks, we recommend creating a Windows System Restore Point. This lets you restore your system if something unexpected happens.
restore.needsAdmin: Creating a restore point needs administrator rights. Restart Panda Tweaks as administrator to do this.
restore.throttled: Windows did not create a new point. By default it only creates one every 24 hours, and a recent one already exists.
restore.protectionDisabled: System Protection is turned off for this drive, so Windows cannot store restore points. You can turn it on in Windows under System Protection.
restore.error: The restore point could not be created.
restore.dontAskHint: You can turn this prompt back on in Settings.
firstrun.intro: A free Windows tweaking tool that shows you exactly what it changes, and can put it back.
firstrun.analyse: Now we will analyse your system. This only reads settings — nothing is changed.
firstrun.langText: Let's set things up. First: your language.
firstrun.themeText: You can change this any time in Settings.
firstrun.rpText: A Windows restore point lets you roll everything back if something goes wrong. Strongly recommended before your first tweaks.
firstrun.rpYesD: Takes about a minute and needs administrator rights
admin.declined: Without approval Panda Tweaks keeps running as a standard user.
admin.explain: Panda Tweaks starts without administrator rights on purpose. It only asks when a change genuinely needs them.
error.applyFailed: This tweak could not be applied.
services.title: Windows Services
services.subtitle: {count} services that can be turned off safely.
services.note: Turning one off sets its start type to Disabled and stops it. Undo restores the start type that was measured beforehand — not an assumed default.
cleanup.title: Cleanup
cleanup.subtitle: Temporary files and caches Windows does not clear on its own.
cleanup.warning: Deleted files are gone — Panda Tweaks cannot undo this. Nothing here is pre-selected.
startup.title: Startup
startup.subtitle: {on} of {total} entries start with Windows.
startup.note: Panda Tweaks writes the same marker Task Manager writes. The entry itself and the shortcut are left untouched — which is why this can be undone.
startup.readFailed: Autostart entries could not be read.
startup.changeFailed: The entry could not be changed.
fixes.title: Fixes
fixes.subtitle: Repair common Windows problems — including ones a tweak caused.
fixes.note: Every repair puts default behaviour back. Each runs on its own and none is pre-selected: a repair you do not need buys you nothing.
fixes.needsAdmin: Most repairs need administrator rights. Without them they stay disabled.
presets.title: Game Presets
presets.subtitle: Ready-made selections built from the existing tweak catalogue.
presets.note: A preset is a named selection, not a separate mechanism. It can only contain what the catalogue can already do on its own — and every tweak stays individually reversible.
presets.unavailableHint: {n} tweaks in this preset need powercfg, netsh or bcdedit. There is no typed operation for those yet, so they are skipped rather than faked.
apply.noneAvailable: None of these can run on this PC — they are all marked unavailable.
apply.unavailableTrimmed: {count} left out: not available on this PC.
apply.noneFit: None of these suit this PC — every one was held back.
apply.unfitTrimmed: {count} left out because of your hardware:
skipped.needsSsd: Your system drive is a hard disk — prefetching actually helps there
skipped.driveUnknown: Cannot tell whether your system drive is an SSD, and this hurts on a hard disk
skipped.needsRam: Not enough RAM for this to be a good trade
skipped.ramUnknown: Cannot read how much RAM this PC has
apply.adminTrimmed: {count} left out: these need administrator rights.
apply.allNeedAdmin: All {count} of these need administrator rights. Restart the app as administrator and try again.
about.communityBody: The build is handed out through Discord and nowhere else — one official file, one place to ask when something goes wrong. The full source is public: every tweak, every registry key and every command is plain text you can read before you run it.
apply.gameRunning: {game} is running. It rewrites its settings file when it closes, so anything changed now would be thrown away. Nothing has been applied — close the game and try again.
drivers.title: Old drivers
drivers.subtitle: Driver packages that a newer version has replaced
drivers.note: Every driver update leaves the old package behind in the driver store, and Windows never removes it. A graphics driver is one to two gigabytes each time.
drivers.onlySuperseded: Only packages with a newer version of themselves already installed are listed. The newest version of every driver stays, and one a device is currently using is never offered.
drivers.notReversible: Removing a package deletes it. There is no undo — Windows would have to download it again.
drivers.none: No superseded driver packages. Nothing to clean up here.
drivers.needsAdmin: Reading the driver store needs administrator rights.
drivers.failed: The driver store could not be read.
drivers.confirmBody: {count} packages, {size}. This cannot be undone: the files are deleted and Windows would have to fetch them again to roll a device back.
